newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thatcher to open HK bridge under tight security.
newsitem.headline: Thatcher to open HK bridge under tight security.

text.p: Thousands of police will be used in a huge security operation in Hong Kong on Sunday when Britain's Margaret Thatcher opens one of the world's biggest bridges.
The former prime minister and colonial Governor Chris Patten will open the spectacular Lantau Link road and railway bridge connecting the British-ruled territory with its future new airport.
Concern about security is running high after cables at the Tsing Ma Bridge were cut last week by saboteurs or vandals.
Police chief Colin Keenan told reporters hundreds of thousands of people were expected to flock to the scene to see a huge fireworks show when the ribbon is cut.

Keenan said police were ready for any guerrilla attack near the 1,377 metre long bridge -- a major part of the US$20 billion Chek Lap Kok airport development on Lantau Island. The airport opens next April.
It will be the last major British-staged spectacles in Hong Kong before the colony of 156 years reverts to Chinese control at midnight on June 30.
"We have made preparations, quite significant preparations in terms of the bridge and the ceremonies", Keenan said.
About 2,500 police would be deployed in the area and a special command unit would act as nerve centre for traffic and crowd control management, he said.
